word_order: SOV — verbs and auxiliaries regularly appear at the end of clauses (e.g., 文末に述べました、できません、語った).
punctuation_present: always — sentence-final and clause punctuation (。 、 「 」 （ ） etc.) appear in every sample
register: newswire / formal written prose (journalistic or encyclopedia-style sentences)
clause_boundary_signals: と（引用の終わりに出る）
ます/ました/ません（敬体語尾）
notes_for_prompt_writer: Segment only where the source shows clause-final morphology or clear closing punctuation; prefer splitting after sentence-final verbs/auxiliaries (ます/た/ない/etc.) or after full stops/closing quotes. Do not rely on spaces (there are none); treat particles like が/の/と/て/から as unstable — avoid splitting immediately after them unless following token confirms a clause end. Always attach closing punctuation and closing quotation/parenthesis marks to the preceding segment.
